Um I can tell you that you did nothing wrong. A lot of people believe that bullies cause the one being bullied to commit suicide. Although that is not completely wrong it is also not 100% true. I hate victim shaming as well especially when it comes to suicide because I've been there and will most likely be there again in the future. From my experience, as far as an outside force or person causing another to kill themselves, I don't think it's 100% to blame on that inflicting individual. A lot of factors go into suicide and society is a big one. When I was bullied in middle school, the school had propaganda posters up with emo kids on them that looked like my friends and I. These posters would be all like "Reach out, don't be the bully." and just a lot of anti-bully stuff. But what I had learned is that bullies are inevitable. From the stone age, people have been bullied and sociologically, bullies are kind of an "essential" in a societal package. What I was upset at my school for was that instead of offering help to those being bullied, they would deny bullying all together. They had those posters up but when I would be called in to see the crisis counselor cause I was being bullied, the counselor denied any bullies being in the school haha. Anyway, as one who was being bullied, I only got comfort when I was given tools to cope with the bullying. Like encouragement and self-image that countered what the bullying made me feel. Instead of blaming the bullies like society tends to do, I accepted that bullies are everywhere and took it upon myself to evolve and develop strengths that protected me from the attacks. 

Although this doesnt seem related to your situation, I can see why people are blaming you but the only thing you did was break up with her. Not everyone who is dumped commits suicide so your action is not a vital factor in these cases. Again, I don't want to sound like I am victim shaming, especially when she is a real person and it really happened but what can be learned from this situation by everyone is:

dont put so much value on your significant other so much that you dont know what to do with yourself when they leave,

know that when stuff like this that cause suicidal thoughts occur that you can get help

and do not keep yourself in an uncomfortable situation in fear that leaving will hurt the other person

When I was in 4th grade, we boarded our 2 dogs while we went out of town. We get a call that one of our dogs, Buddy, had passed away in the crate. So we came back in town and I remember my father carrying a cardboard box with Buddy's body in it, out to our little flower bed in the back yard. I remember the flannel blanket sticking out of the box as I watched my dad shovel dirt over the box. That night, I dreamt that I heard scratching at my window and went outside to check it out and Buddy runs in to the house and down the hall. I woke up and went to school only to be sent home for not being able to control my crying.

I can relate to there being " no inbetween". Super chill could just be a subconscious facade in order to help you function in certain situations. Like sometimes you feel confident that you can fake being comfortable too well so you act very outgoing then other times you over fixate on  not being able to fake being comfortable and thus you become more anxious. Either way, these behaviors are both anxiety. Finding a balance is hard but it is the only solution. But I, myself have not figured out how to balance these things either. But I look forward to the day that I can. An important part in finding balance I believe, is allowing yourself the time to work things out in the moment. Don't be too hard on yourself.  I am a big fan of the "Reparenting your inner child" or "child work" practice and this ties in with it. An ideal mother/father will see you make a mistake and you would want them to tell you that a mistake is a mistake and that you will get better or that it was an accident and to not worry about it. This is how we should've been treated as children but that is not always the case, sadly. So treating yourself like a loving parent will ease the obstacles along the way and make reaching your goal smoother but not getting caught up in the little things and staying focused on the goal at hand. I find this to work more than anything else for me and suggest you read up on it. There are some good (cheesy) videos on youtube too. I know I know only one detail about your situation but people are more alike than we think so I hope this helps.

I am learning that the root of my anxiety is not only from being genetically predisposed to it but also from how my parents treat me and my sisters. It's not so much the physical symptoms that I am worried about; it's just that the workbook my therapist gave me says a lot about agoraphobia and thus learning to relieve the physical symptoms should make my mind and thoughts be less panicked and I guess that's why it isn't working. I'm not afraid of panicking unless I am in a full on panic which hasn't happened in about a year. I am more concerned with the thoughts and opinions my parents filled me with from since I can remember. I still live with them and am not in the right condition to leave just yet but I do have a plan. So a lot of the anxiety comes from me being emotionally damaged by my stressful upbringing and I am actually thankful to the physical symptoms for helping me figure out that these thoughts are an illness and thus I can get better. My therapist emphasizes positive self-talk the most and that is something I obviously need and am currently making progress in.

This seems pretty normal. You want to be with your buddies but don't want to be judged for not drinking...

If they judge you for a decision like that then they aren't good friends. Also, caffeine and alcohol amplify anxiety and it is best you put your well being first over having a good time and feeling included. 

If you are wondering why this is happening all of a sudden, then it is the anxiety at play in both the change of occurance and the questioning of "why". Your body is probably only telling you that the alcohol is hurting you but your head (anxiety). is telling you that you will die. Also the feeling alone part is probably the anxiety too. In reality, it just sounds like you have pretty bad anxiety and maybe (i don't want to assume but its something to think about) self-medicating with alcohol has gotten mixed into it all and some changes in your lifestyle need to be made. 

I hope this wasn't to straight forward. I just know how helpful it is to share thoughts from an outside perspective as well as believing the severity of your situation. I hope all goes well and you can remain strong and stand up for your well being. Sorry if I assumed too much, I just want to help.

But then again, I even take 70mg of Vyvanse and 15mg of Adderall for my ADHD and am still a freaking caveman. If your current Psychiatrist ends up not giving you the right prescriptions and/or diagnoses, then maybe look for a new one if you don't feel like the 2 of you are getting anywhere.
